name: Forms of Bhairava with parts, set forth as provisional (VBT 2-13)

definitions.definition: The ninefold form, the mass of sounds, the three-headed form, the triad of powers, nāda-bindu and the rest (2-4) are said in truth not to be Bhairava (11-12); the forms with parts are unsubstantial like a magic show (9), described for meditation for the confused (10), and set forth like sweets from a mother to induce engagement (13).

name: The supreme state of Bhairava (Bhairavī, Parā) in the Vijñānabhairava

definitions.definition: Free of any reckoning of direction and time, not distinguished by place, impossible to designate (14); inner self-experience of bliss, thought-free and full, called Bhairavī (15); a spotless body filling the universe in which there is no one to worship (16); the same is called Parā, the Goddess (17).

name: Power not different from its possessor (VBT 18-21)

definitions.definition: Between power and its possessor non-difference always stands (18); the burning power of fire is not seen as separate from fire (19); Śiva is known through Śakti as directions are known by a lamp or the sun (21).

name: The supportless mind (nirādhāra) in the Vijñānabhairava

definitions.definition: Many of the means end in making the mind or awareness supportless (80, 91, 92, 108, 119, 128, 131), and meditation itself is defined as the supportless, formless, unmoving understanding (146).

name: Awareness as the same in all bodies and everywhere (VBT 100-107, 116)

definitions.definition: The nature of consciousness is in all bodies with no difference anywhere (100); the practitioner contemplates 'I am everywhere' (104), feels awareness in another's body as in one's own (107), and sees that wherever the mind goes there is the state of Śiva (116).

name: The waveless state (nistaraṅga) and its hundred and twelve teachings

definitions.definition: One becomes waveless by abandoning at once whatever the mind goes to (129); the means from v.24 to v.138 are summed at v.139 as a hundred and twelve teachings of the waveless state.

name: Japa, meditation, worship, oblation, sacrifice and bathing as inner acts (VBT 143-153)

definitions.definition: Asked who is repeated, meditated on, worshipped, satisfied (143-144), Bhairava says outer procedure is for the gross (144) and gives inner senses: japa is repeated contemplation of the supreme state (145), dhyāna the unmoving supportless understanding (146), pūjā the firm understanding in the thought-free great space (147), homa the offering of elements, senses and objects with the mind into the fire of the great void (149), yāga satisfaction marked by bliss (150), snāna entering one's own nature (152); where all is one there is no worship (153).

name: Secrecy and worthy recipients of the teaching (VBT 157-160)

definitions.definition: The teaching is never to be revealed to anyone (157), not to another's disciple, the wicked, the cruel or one without devotion to the teacher's feet (158), but to devotees, heroes of thought-free mind and the teacher's circle (158-159); worldly holdings are to be given up for it (159-160).

name: The one established in a means (VBT 140-142, 148)

definitions.definition: Established in any one of the means one becomes Bhairava himself, his word accomplishing deeds, a giver of curse and favour (140); ageless and deathless with aṇimā and other qualities (141); released while living, unstained while acting (142); from day to day the state of fullness arises (148). The text does not say whether these are literal or praise.
